existing_rules: preserve; create CLAUDE.md imports only when absent; project status warns while neither CLAUDE.md nor .claude/CLAUDE.md imports .agf/managed/project-rules.md
version_requirement: Direct AGENTS.md support requires Claude Code v2.1.277+ and appropriate settings; CLAUDE.md import remains a compatibility option
rules_observed: 2026-11-16, Claude Code 2.1.325 with default settings: a fresh session did not load AGENTS.md by itself; it loaded .agf/managed/project-rules.md only after CLAUDE.md imported it
managed_copy: Generated skill copies originate from the same framework source; do not edit copies independently

permissions.installation: not installed by project install; replace the placeholder path, review the rules and merge them into the project's settings; with the placeholder left in place the Edit and Write rules protect nothing
permissions.scope: loaded only when Claude Code starts in that project directory; a session started in a parent directory does not use a subdirectory's .claude/settings.json
observed: 2026-11-16, Claude Code 2.1.325 on Linux, headless sessions in throwaway directories; each case ran once
a Read rule refused Read, Glob and Grep
Edit and Write rules refused Edit and Write; cp into the protected path was refused while cp into another directory ran
a python3 -c one-liner wrote into the protected path
Bash(git push:*), Bash(gh pr create:*) and Bash(glab mr create:*) refused those commands, --help included; git -C . push did not match and ran
a subdirectory's .claude/settings.json was unused when the session started in its parent
with user-level settings loaded (they included a command-rewriting hook) a Bash(git push:*) allow rule did not apply, and without them it did; the cause was not isolated
with Bash missing from the allowed tools, read-only find and head still ran in the working directory, cat ../outside.txt was refused, and --disallowedTools Bash removed the tool
--restricted confined Read and Glob to the working directory
not_observed: shell redirection: under a Bash(echo:*) allow rule it was refused even into an unprotected directory, so whether the Write rule alone stops it is unknown
